evidence.functional_evidence: The hosted app can create an election but has no UI for add_voter, open, vote, tally or get_winner (Owned/Enrolled pages are mocks). After a winner is declared the creator can reopen the election, so the stored winner goes stale.

limitations: The Create Election page is the only page that talks to the program. Owned Elections and Enrolled Elections are static mock UIs (hard-coded 'President' / 'Secretary' and '42' voters; the Get Winners button has no handler). There is no UI for add_voter, toggle_election, vote, tally_votes or get_winner, even though the Create Election copy says you will add voters on Owned Elections. Those instructions are covered by the script.

The app's createElection always passes maxPositions=10, maxCandidatesPerPosition=10 and an empty voter list (utils/solana.ts). An election created through the app therefore has no allowed voters until add_voter is called, which the UI never does.
Elections start closed (is_open = false). Voting is rejected with ElectionIsClosed until the authority calls toggle_election, which the app never does.

toggle_election has no finished state: after get_winner, the authority can reopen, add voters (add_voter is only blocked while the election is open) and accept new votes. The stored winners stay stale until get_winner is called again. The script reopened, added W, and W voted Abstain for President: the counts became Alice:1 Abstain:1, but winners still read President=Alice (tx 5ySN2epW…).
tally_votes only writes the counts to the program log; it does not store winners. Abstain is a real candidate and can win — in the script, Treasurer=Abstain because V voted Abstain and Bob had 0.

The form's submit loop calls addCandidate(electionName, i, name) with i equal to the position's index in the form, so two candidates under one position both go to that position (the UI run added Alice and Bob to President, which the program accepts because the app's max is 10). Sending uses window.solana directly (not the wallet-adapter provider) against a hardcoded Connection to api.devnet.solana.com.
The static export shows React hydration warnings (#418, #423) on first load; they are cosmetic and did not block the four program transactions.
